visibility.reason: The canonical capability vocabulary describes platform serving and the SDK coverage vocabulary only accepts covered or partial. Neither can represent an unavailable Zarr client and a deliberately withheld sample without implying an executable SDK surface.

server.summary: Registration, bounded subset reads, CoverageJSON serving, WCS fixture paths, and datacube tile components exist, but the repository does not contain a positive public live Zarr canary covering the end-to-end serving claim.

client.summary: The JavaScript SDK exposes no Zarr package, connector, metadata reader, slice reader, or tile client.

sample.summary: No runnable or published Zarr sample is allowed until the public fixture, live service, and SDK publication gates pass.

evidence.claim: Maps the versioned Zarr administration route family and refresh operation.
Exercises the register, list, get, and delete lifecycle through HTTP.
Registers Zarr services in the server composition root.

serverEvidence.boundary: The lifecycle test proves the administration contract, not a readable public cloud-hosted store or a successful refresh against object storage.

evidence.claim: Binds registered Zarr stores to the OGC API Coverages service.
Plans and returns a bounded CoverageJSON subset.
Proves chunk-aware bounded subset reads with pinned in-memory fixtures.

serverEvidence.boundary: The service and reader are fixture-evidenced, but no Zarr-specific positive OGC API Coverages HTTP round trip or public live response is recorded in the audited proof.

evidence.claim: Maps the public datacube tile route to a registered Zarr coverage slice.
Proves that the HTTP route exists and returns 404 without a servable registration.
Records route coverage plus planner and renderer component evidence.

serverEvidence.boundary: The checked-in endpoint test is negative-path only; planner and PNG renderer tests do not replace a positive registered-store HTTP or live canary.

serverEvidence.route: WCS 2.0.1 GetCoverage through ImageServer and service routes

evidence.claim: Exercises positive registered-Zarr PNG slices and explicit unsupported cases through HTTP.

serverEvidence.boundary: The fixture path supports bounded native-CRS single-coordinate PNG slices; TIFF and range-subset composition are explicitly unsupported.

versions: Zarr v2 reads .zgroup, .zattrs, and .zarray; grouped discovery depends on an optional attributes variables manifest.
Zarr v3 reads root and child zarr.json nodes; grouped discovery depends on the root attributes variables list and is not general store enumeration.
codecs: Tested reads cover v2 uncompressed and zlib chunks plus v3 uncompressed and gzip chunks.
v3 zstd, blosc, sharding_indexed, crc32c, and unknown codecs are rejected.
Zarr filters, Fortran order, big-endian values, and unsupported non-numeric data types are rejected.
layout: C-order regular chunk grids are supported.
v3 default c-prefixed chunk keys and v2-style dotted chunk keys are recognized.
Coordinates depend on Honua attributes for variables, dimension names, extent, and CRS rather than unrestricted CF/Zarr metadata inference.
crs: Server georeferencing reads the Honua crs_wkid and extent attributes when present.
Datacube tile requests require the tile matrix set SRID to equal the coverage storage SRID.
Cross-CRS reprojection of a Zarr tile window is not implemented.
budgets: Metadata documents are capped at 64 KiB and discovery is capped at 64 variables.
The subset reader caps a request at 4096 chunks and 256 MiB decoded data.
OGC API Coverage output is capped at 16 MiB decoded data and a datacube tile slice at 4 MiB decoded data.

publicFixture.requirement: Publish a redistributable immutable fixture URL, license, SHA-256 digest, expected metadata, and expected subset and tile digests.
Cover one supported Zarr v2 store and one supported Zarr v3 store, including codec, CRS, spatial, temporal, vertical, and named-dimension expectations.
Record deterministic byte-range traces proving chunk-bounded reads and rejection at declared request limits.

liveService.requirement: Record a deployed server commit and capability manifest that advertise the exact Zarr-backed routes under test.
Fetch one bounded Zarr-backed OGC API Coverage subset from a public deployment and verify media type, byte limit, axes, shape, and digest.
Fetch one Zarr-backed datacube PNG tile from a public deployment and verify media type, dimensions, byte limit, and digest.

sdkPublication.requirement: Pin a versioned server contract that resolves registration, metadata, subset, tile, version, codec, coordinate, and CRS semantics.
Implement typed metadata, slice, and tile operations with explicit byte and chunk budgets, cancellation, auth, request interception, and typed unsupported-format errors.
Pass deterministic fixture contracts and scheduled live evidence without adding unsupported codecs or coordinate inference.

samplePublication.requirement: Publish a runnable sample only after the SDK package export exists and both fixture and live evidence gates pass.

operations.responsibility: Describe groups, arrays, named dimensions, chunks, data types, codecs, fill values, coordinates, CRS, and consolidated-metadata availability without downloading array payloads.
Read an explicitly bounded spatial, temporal, vertical, or named-dimension slice using chunk-aware range requests and return a typed multidimensional result.
Request a bounded server-rendered datacube tile or adapt an explicitly supported two-dimensional slice to a renderer without hiding CRS or resampling constraints.

crossCutting: Cancellation and authentication flow through the shared request pipeline.
Request interception exposes every metadata, range, subset, and tile request.
Byte, chunk, dimension, and decoded-output budgets default closed and are observable.
Unsupported versions, codecs, coordinates, and CRS transformations fail with typed errors.
Direct object-store access and Honua server operations remain distinct execution modes.

externalVocabulary.gap: The canonical keys name server capabilities, while config/sdk-coverage.schema.json only allows covered or partial SDK entries with executable entrypoints and evidence. It has no unavailable, blocked, or withheld state and no client-specific Zarr key.
externalVocabulary.promotionRule: Do not add Zarr to the support manifest, SDK coverage crosswalk, package exports, public capability projection, or sample catalog until an executable client and its required evidence exist.
